what: Local Pooled Error-Based ANOVA for RNA-Seq Count Data
title: Local Pooled Error-Based ANOVA for RNA-Seq Count Data
text: LPEseq2 R package differential expression analysis RNA-seq count data using local pooled error-based ANOVA conventional ANOVA, supporting one-way multi-way (interaction-free) designs. Many RNA-seq studies — including pilot experiments, rare clinical sample studies, reanalyses public datasets — limited one two biological replicates per condition. constraint especially common single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq), high per-sample cost library preparation sequencing often restricts number biological donors one two per condition, even large numbers cells profiled. low-replicate conditions, conventional differential expression methods DESeq2 edgeR may produce unreliable results fail run, per-gene dispersion estimation becomes unstable. LPEseq2 addresses borrowing variance information across genes similar expression intensities rather estimating per gene independently, making applicable even one replicate per group available. LPEseq2 supports LPE-ANOVA small-sample RNA-seq data, standard gene-wise ANOVA larger sample sizes, automatic mode selects analysis method based group sample size. design can one-way (~ group) multi-way multiple main-effect factors interaction terms (~ genotype + treatment); see Multi-way (-interaction) designs. LPEseq2 also provides Seurat-integrated pseudo-bulk workflow cell-type-resolved differential expression analysis annotated scRNA-seq data. particularly useful number biological donors per condition small conventional pseudo-bulk methods. LPEseq2 intended complementary exploratory tool, replacement established methods DESeq2, edgeR, limma-voom adequate replication available. p-values adjusted p-values produced LPEseq2 treated approximate candidate-gene ranking measures rather calibrated false discovery rate guarantees. Biological follow-validation recommended. can also run LPEseq2 directly browser without installation: Launch LPEseq2 Shiny Web Tool

what: Seurat object input for pseudo-bulk analysis
title: Local Pooled Error-Based ANOVA for RNA-Seq Count Data
text: pseudo-bulk analysis, input annotated Seurat object raw counts cell-level metadata. Seurat object contain metadata columns sample ID, condition, cell type annotation. metadata column names can customized using sample_col, condition_col, celltype_col arguments. Pseudo-bulk count matrices generated summing raw counts across cells within sample cell type. Normalized log-normalized expression values used pseudo-bulk aggregation. Two aggregation modes supported:
code: seurat_obj$sample_id seurat_obj$condition seurat_obj$celltype

title: Local Pooled Error-Based ANOVA for RNA-Seq Count Data
text: cell numbers substantially unequal across samples within cell type, normalize_by_ncells option can used reduce imbalance. normalize_by_ncells = TRUE, sample’s aggregated count vector scaled per-ncells_scale-cells basis. equivalent computing CP1K (Counts per 1K Cells) ncells_scale = 1000 (default): equalizes contribution sample regardless cell count, particularly important rare cell types cell counts differ markedly across samples. Normalization method compatibility: normalize_by_ncells = TRUE produces non-integer values. Therefore, TMM DESeq2 normalization automatically disabled require raw integer counts. library_size normalization remains available can combined normalize_by_ncells = TRUE additionally correct sequencing depth differences cell-number scaling: normalize_by_ncells = TRUE normalize.method = "none" (default TMM/DESeq2 specified), cell-number imbalance corrected. Sequencing depth differences remain uncorrected. min.count threshold adjusted match scaled count values (example, min.count = 1 instead default 5).
code: CP1K = (sum of raw counts across cells) / n_cells × 1000      = raw_count / (n_cells / ncells_scale) # Correct for both cell-number imbalance and sequencing depth res_pb <- LPE_pseudobulk(   seurat_obj = seurat_obj,   method = "sample",   normalize_by_ncells = TRUE,   ncells_scale = 1000,   normalize.method = "library_size",   # additionally correct for sequencing depth   min.count = 1,   ... )

title: Local Pooled Error-Based ANOVA for RNA-Seq Count Data
code: library(LPEseq2)  set.seed(123)  counts <- matrix(   rnbinom(1000, mu = 50, size = 10),   nrow = 100,   ncol = 10 )  rownames(counts) <- paste0("gene", 1:100) colnames(counts) <- paste0("sample", 1:10)  colData <- data.frame(   group = rep(c("Control", "Treatment"), each = 5),   row.names = colnames(counts) )  prep <- LPE_preprocess(   counts = counts,   colData = colData,   design = ~ group,   normalize.method = "library_size",   verbose = FALSE )  res <- LPE_ANOVA(   object = prep,   analysis.method = "auto",   standard.min.group.n = 5,   n.bin = 100,   df = 10,   use_weighted_between = FALSE,   p.method = "chisq",   verbose = FALSE )  head(res) attr(res, "analysis.method")

what: Pseudo-bulk analysis from an annotated Seurat object
title: Local Pooled Error-Based ANOVA for RNA-Seq Count Data
text: recommended pseudo-bulk workflow aggregate raw counts sample--cell-type level run LPEseq2 separately cell type. cell numbers substantially unequal across samples within cell type, use normalize_by_ncells = TRUE scale sample’s counts CP1K (per-1000-cells) basis analysis: Note: normalize_by_ncells = TRUE, TMM DESeq2 normalization automatically disabled require raw integer counts. Use normalize.method = "library_size" "none" combination normalize_by_ncells = TRUE. combined result across analyzed cell types can accessed : Cell-type-specific results can accessed : Pseudo-bulk metadata diagnostic information can checked : selected cell types analyzed, use celltypes argument:
code: library(LPEseq2)  # Standard pseudo-bulk (raw integer counts, library_size normalization) res_pb <- LPE_pseudobulk(   seurat_obj = seurat_obj,   method = "sample",   assay = "RNA",   counts_layer = "counts",   sample_col = "sample_id",   condition_col = "condition",   celltype_col = "celltype",   min_cells = 10,   normalize.method = "library_size",   analysis.method = "auto",   standard.min.group.n = 5,   n.bin = 100,   df = 10,   trim.method = "iqr",   p.method = "chisq",   verbose = TRUE ) # Cell-number-normalized pseudo-bulk (CP1K scaling) res_pb_norm <- LPE_pseudobulk(   seurat_obj = seurat_obj,   method = "sample",   assay = "RNA",   counts_layer = "counts",   sample_col = "sample_id",   condition_col = "condition",   celltype_col = "celltype",   min_cells = 10,   normalize_by_ncells = TRUE,       # scale to CP1K (per-1000-cells) basis   ncells_scale = 1000,   normalize.method = "library_size", # additionally correct for sequencing depth   min.count = 1,                     # adjust threshold for scaled count values   analysis.method = "auto",   standard.min.group.n = 5,   n.bin = 100,   df = 10,   trim.method = "iqr",   p.method = "chisq",   verbose = TRUE ) all_res <- res_pb$combined_result head(all_res) names(res_pb$results_by_celltype)  cd4_res <- res_pb$results_by_celltype$CD4_T head(cd4_res) cd4_meta <- res_pb$metadata_by_celltype$CD4_T head(cd4_meta)  res_pb$diagnostics$CD4_T res_pb$errors res_cd4 <- LPE_pseudobulk(   seurat_obj = seurat_obj,   method = "sample",   celltypes = c("CD4_T"),   sample_col = "sample_id",   condition_col = "condition",   celltype_col = "celltype" )

text: design LPE_preprocess() accepts one main-effect term, e.g. ~ genotype + treatment. Interaction terms (:B *B) supported raise error, since LPE variance-trend / test-statistic machinery assumes additive model. design term’s main effect tested Type II sum--squares decomposition (comparing full additive model model term dropped), order-independent main-effects-design. one-way design, result columns unsuffixed (MS_between, F, p.value, q.value, …) exactly . multi-way design, one set columns reported per term, suffixed term name, e.g.: variance.eval = "per_group" (Welch-style, per-group variance evaluation) supported one-way designs; raises error multi-way designs; use variance.eval = "grand_mean" (default) instead. attr(res, "design.terms") reports design term names tested. Column names syntactically valid R names (example time point, containing space) can used design backquoted, e.g. ~ genotype +time point`; output columns namedF_time point,q.value_time point`, .
code: colData_mw <- data.frame(   genotype  = rep(rep(c("wt", "mut"), each = 2), times = 2),   treatment = rep(c("control", "drug"), each = 4),   row.names = colnames(counts_mw) )  prep_mw <- LPE_preprocess(   counts = counts_mw,   colData = colData_mw,   design = ~ genotype + treatment,   normalize.method = "library_size",   verbose = FALSE )  res_mw <- LPE_ANOVA(   object = prep_mw,   analysis.method = "auto",   standard.min.group.n = 5,   verbose = FALSE )  head(res_mw) gene, mean, var, MS_between_genotype, F_genotype, p.value_genotype, q.value_genotype, MS_between_treatment, F_treatment, p.value_treatment, q.value_treatment, method

title: Local Pooled Error-Based ANOVA for RNA-Seq Count Data
text: LPEseq2 supports IQR-based fixed-threshold (dvalue) outlier trimming pairwise values used variance trend estimation. default trim.method = "auto" selects "none" "dvalue" described Automatic variance-training settings. trim.method = "iqr", LPEseq2 first pools within-group pairwise values -group-derived values. pooled values divided expression-intensity -bins, conventional boxplot rule applied within bin: trim.method = "dvalue", LPEseq2 removes pairwise value whose M value (rescaled difference used variance estimation) exceeds d.threshold / sqrt(2) absolute value, prior variance trend estimation. Thresholding M rather raw D keeps cutoff equally strict regardless within- vs. -group origin group size. reproduces outlier-removal step LPEseq1’s non-replicate analysis (Gim et al. 2016), equivalent M value thresholded fixed value (default d.threshold = 1.2, .e. |M| ≤ 0.849) chosen empirically via reproducibility analysis across benchmark datasets. Users verify whether default appropriate normalization scale log-transform. Outlier detection performed M-value scale M scale used local pooled variance estimation.

title: Run LPE-ANOVA — LPE_ANOVA
text: object list returned LPE_preprocess(). n.bin Number quantile bins used variance trend estimation. df Degrees freedom smoothing spline. trim.method Outlier trimming method applied pairwise values used variance trend estimation. One "auto" (default), "dvalue", "iqr", "none". "auto" chooses replication (see Automatic variance-training settings Details): "none" every design cell least two samples, otherwise "dvalue". See LPE_ANOVA_var trimming rules. use_weighted_between "auto" (default), TRUE FALSE. Whether include weighted -group differences variance trend estimation. "auto" uses FALSE every design cell least two samples (replicate pairs ), otherwise TRUE. d.threshold Numeric. Threshold LPEseq1 raw-D scale, used derive fixed M-scale cutoff (d.threshold/sqrt(2)) applied trim.method = "dvalue". Default 1.2, matching default reported LPEseq1 (Gim et al. 2016). Ignored trim.method values. See LPE_ANOVA_var details. analysis.method Analysis method. One "LPE", "standard_anova", "auto". "LPE" uses local pooled error-based ANOVA. "standard_anova" uses conventional gene-wise ANOVA (Type II sums squares multi-way designs). "auto" selects standard ANOVA every factor-level combination (design "cell") least standard.min.group.n samples; otherwise, LPE-ANOVA used. standard.min.group.n Minimum per-cell sample size required use standard ANOVA analysis.method = "auto". "cell" unique combination design factor levels (one-way design, simply group). verbose Logical. Whether print progress messages. p.method P-value calculation method. One "chisq" "F_inf". variance.eval Character string specifying fitted variance trend evaluated test statistic. One "grand_mean" "per_group". "grand_mean" (default) evaluates variance trend gene's overall (grand) mean expression uses single pooled variance test statistic; mode supports one-way multi-way (main-effects-) designs. "per_group" evaluates variance trend separately group's mean expression combines group-specific variances via inverse-variance weighting Welch-type unequal-variance test statistic (returned method = "LPE_Welch" different var/MS_between definition; see Details). "per_group" supported one-way designs (single design term); raises error multi-way designs.

title: LPEseq2 0.0.1
text: Shiny web tool (app.R): single “Group variable” dropdown replaced dynamic set dropdowns controlled “+” / “-” buttons, several testing-group factors can added design (~ + B + ..., interaction). Selections preserved factor added, new dropdown defaults first unused metadata column, duplicate / NA / single-level selections give clear message, “Variance evaluation” restricted grand_mean one factor chosen. design formula built backquoted names, metadata columns containing spaces now work (also one-way analyses). LPE_preprocess() / LPE_ANOVA() / standard_ANOVA_expr(): design variables non-syntactic names (e.g. time point) supported multi-way formulas via backquotes; output columns use plain name (F_time point). LPE_preprocess() / LPE_ANOVA() / standard_ANOVA_expr(): added support multi-way (main-effects-) designs. design can now formula one term, e.g. ~ genotype + treatment, addition one-way ~ group. Interaction terms (:B *B) supported raise error, since LPE variance-trend / test-statistic machinery assumes additive model. design term’s main effect tested via Type II sum--squares decomposition (RSS model term dropped, minus RSS full model), order-independent additive design reduces exactly original one-way computation single term (verified numerically identical). one-way design, LPE_ANOVA() output columns unchanged (MS_between, F, p.value, q.value, …); multi-way design, one suffixed set columns reported per design term (e.g. F_genotype, p.value_genotype, F_treatment, p.value_treatment, …). LPE_preprocess()’s returned list gains factors field (named list individual design factors); group kept backward compatibility now represents crossing design factors (identical single factor one-way designs). variance.eval = "per_group" (Welch-style) remains one-way raises informative error multi-way designs; analysis.method = "auto" now bases group-size check minimum factor-level combination (“cell”) size. LPE_ANOVA_var() unchanged. LPE_ANOVA_var(): pairwise D/M values used intensity-dependent variance trend estimation now symmetrized ±D trimming quantile binning, matching LPEseq1’s original approach (Gim et al. 2016) fixing difference distribution’s center zero. changes variance estimation formula data-estimated-mean variance known-mean (zero) variance, shift var, F, p.value, q.value LPE_ANOVA() results (LPE-ANOVA mode) compared previous versions. trim.info pairwise counts (n_total_before, n_within_before, n_between_before, _after/_removed counterparts) now twice number underlying pairs. LPE_pseudobulk() now supports trim.method = "dvalue" d.threshold argument, matching LPE_ANOVA() / LPE_ANOVA_var(). Previously "iqr" "none" available pseudobulk level even though "dvalue" already implemented underlying LPE_ANOVA_var(). LPE_ANOVA() / LPE_ANOVA_var() / LPE_pseudobulk(): trim.method default changed "iqr" "dvalue". LPE_ANOVA() / LPE_ANOVA_var() / LPE_pseudobulk(): use_weighted_between default changed FALSE TRUE. LPE_ANOVA() gained variance.eval argument ("grand_mean" (default) "per_group"), controlling whether intensity-dependent variance evaluated grand mean separately per group (Welch-style, equivalent LPEseq1’s Z-test k = 2). LPE_ANOVA_var(): trim.method = "dvalue" now applies threshold M scale (d.threshold / sqrt(2)) instead raw D scale. previous raw-D thresholding, effective strictness outlier removal -group pairs became lenient group sample size increased; thresholding M keeps cutoff equally strict regardless group size, numerically identical previous behavior groups exactly one sample (LPEseq1’s original design).
